items.title: Section: Three Abidings Through Emptiness, Wishlessness, and Signlessness — And Six Practices That Make the Teaching Truly One's Own

items.zh: 復次，有諸苾芻住三種住、行六正行，於大師教多有所作。謂住解脫住、住解脫門住，及住能引解脫門法住。行無間行、行善受思惟行、行修所引善根生起行、行離諸愛味簡擇諦行、行即於此無增上慢行、行正清淨受用行。
items.en:
Second, through abiding and practice; first, stating. Furthermore, monks who abide in three kinds of abiding and practice six correct practices accomplish a great deal within the Teacher's instruction.
Second, listing them. Namely, abiding in liberation, abiding in the gateway to liberation, and abiding in the dharma giving rise to that gateway.
[The six practices, listed together:] the practice of uninterrupted activity, the practice of properly receiving reflection, the practice of wholesome roots arising through cultivation, the practice of discerning all conditioned phenomena free from relishing attachment, the practice of freedom from over-estimation within this very practice, and the practice of correctly, purely receiving its benefit.

items.title: Section: Two Kinds of Giving, Its Twofold Fruit, and Pūrṇa's Serene Endurance Under Abuse

items.zh: 復次，有二種捨施。一、受者捨施，二、施者捨施。施果亦有二種。一、得大財富，二、得此等流受用勝解。
items.en:
Third, through giving; first, subsumed by cause. Furthermore, there are two kinds of giving: first, the recipient's giving; second, the giver's giving.
Second, subsumed by fruit. The fruit of giving is likewise twofold: first, obtaining great wealth; second, obtaining the resulting predisposition towards its continued enjoyment.

items.title: Section: Opening the Debate Against the Sarvāstivādin — Why "Real in All Three Times" Cannot Withstand Six Searching Questions

items.zh: 復次，當辨證成道理。問：依何道理，應知宣說唯從未來非實非有諸行相生？答：若未來法行相實有而得生者，此法為轉而說生耶？謂從未來世處，轉向現在世處。
items.en:
Third, deciding the three times and four conditions; first, stating and distinguishing. Furthermore, one should now establish the correct account of this matter.
Second, establishing it; first, explaining the principle; first, refuting the alternate view; first, raising the claim that phenomena arise moving from the future towards the present; first, the question. Question: by what principle should one understand that phenomena arise solely from a future that is neither ultimately real nor truly existent?
Second, the answer; first, interrogating the meaning; first, the meaning of transformed arising; first, stating the challenge. Answer: if the characteristic of a future phenomenon is truly, really existent, and it then arises, does this phenomenon merely transform in order to be said to arise?
Second, explaining the meaning. Namely: does it move from its place in the future world over into its place in the present world?

items.title: Section: Five More Challenges to "Real in All Three Times" — Death, Condition, Function, Completion, and Distinct Characteristic

items.zh: 為死生耶？謂未來世死，生現在世。為彼為緣而得生耶？謂於未來法住不變，用彼為緣，於現在世有餘法生。為有業用而說生耶？謂於未來本無業用，至現在世方有業用。為圓滿相而說生耶？謂於未來相未圓滿，至現在世相乃圓滿。為由異相而說生耶？謂於未來，有未來分及有因分，由此二種其相有異。來至現在，有現在分及有果分，由此二種其相有異。
items.en:
Second, the meaning of death-and-arising; first, stating the challenge: does it arise through dying? Second, explaining the meaning: the future dies, and the present arises.
Third, the meaning of conditioned arising; first, stating the challenge: does it arise by taking that future as its condition? Second, explaining the meaning: the future phenomenon abides unchanged, and, taking it as condition, some further phenomenon arises in the present.
Fourth, the meaning of functional arising; first, stating the challenge: is it said to arise through possessing functional efficacy? Second, explaining the meaning: the future originally lacks functional efficacy, which is possessed only upon reaching the present.
Fifth, the meaning of completed arising; first, stating the challenge: is it said to arise through a completed characteristic? Second, explaining the meaning: the future characteristic is not yet complete, and becomes complete only upon reaching the present.
Sixth, the meaning of distinct-characteristic arising; first, stating the challenge: is it said to arise through a distinct characteristic? Second, explaining the meaning; first, regarding the future: the future has both a future portion and a causal portion, these two differing in characteristic. Second, regarding the present: upon reaching the present, there is both a present portion and a resultant portion, these two likewise differing in characteristic.

items.title: Section: Refuting All Six — None of the Sarvāstivādin's Own Answers Can Explain How the Future Becomes Present

items.zh: 如是六種諸法生起，皆不應理。何以故？非無方無處法，有從異方轉趣異方義。亦非未生未已生法，而有死義。若彼為緣而得生者，便異法生，非未來生，此於未來便為未有。又一切法，第一義中無作用故，業用離相異不可得，唯即於相而假建立。設有異者，未來、現在同實有相，唯說現在獨有業用，理不可得。又此業用，便應本無而今得生。又與世尊微妙言說即成相違。如說：諸行非常、非恒。汝顯諸行業用無常，由此義故行應是常又，等於一相。若相異分得是有者，相之異分何故不有。又相異分本無今有，相之異分何故不成本無今有。又離色等一切行相，餘未來分必不可得。又應未來無有果相，現在方有果相生起。
items.en:
Second, refuting each; first, a blanket rejection: all six of these accounts of how phenomena arise are unreasonable.
Second, refuting them individually; first, the challenge posed: why? Second, the refutations; first, refuting mere transformation: what has neither location nor place cannot coherently be said to move from one place to another.
Second, refuting death-and-arising: nor can what has not yet arisen at all be said to die.
Third, refuting conditioned arising: if the present arises by taking that future as its condition, then a distinct phenomenon arises, not the future's own arising — this future thereby becomes, on your own account, non-existent.
Fourth, refuting functional arising; first, the refutation that only the present truly has function: moreover, all phenomena, in ultimate truth, are without function, since function apart from characteristic is unobtainable and is only conventionally established relative to characteristic. Granting a distinction, if future and present share an equally real characteristic, there is no coherent way that only the present should uniquely possess function. Second, the refutation of originally-absent-now-present: moreover, this function would then have to be originally absent and now arisen.
Fifth, refuting completed arising: moreover, this directly contradicts the Blessed One's own subtle teaching, which states that conditioned things are neither permanent nor eternal. Your claim that the function of conditioned things is impermanent thereby entails, by this very reasoning, that conditioned things themselves must be permanent, collapsing into a single characteristic.
Sixth, refuting distinct-characteristic arising; first, a blanket refutation of the distinct portion; first, refuting the thesis itself: if a distinct portion of characteristic is held to exist, why should not that distinct portion's own distinct portion likewise exist? Second, refuting its supporting reason: moreover, if the distinct portion of characteristic is originally absent and now present, why does not the distinct portion of that distinct portion likewise become originally absent and now present?
Second, refuting the distinct portion individually; first, refuting the future's causal portion: moreover, apart from form and the rest of all conditioned characteristics, no further future portion can ever be obtained. Second, refuting the present's resultant portion: moreover, the future would then have no resultant characteristic at all, and only the present would have a resultant characteristic arising.

items.title: Section: Future and Past Alike Are Not Truly Real — Only the Present Momentarily Abides

items.zh: 如是已辨證成道理。依此道理，應知宣說未來諸法一切行相非實非有，本無今有。如於未來，如是過去，隨其所應，由此道理，當知宣說非實非有。復次，過去行云何？謂相已滅沒，自性已捨。現在行云何？謂相未滅沒，自性未捨，生時暫住。未來行云何？謂因現有，自相未生，未得自性。
items.en:
Third, the conclusion. Having thus established this reasoning, one should know accordingly that all characteristics of future phenomena are neither ultimately real nor truly existent, originally absent and only now coming to be.
Second, extending this to the past's movement from the present. As with the future, so with the past, appropriately adjusted; by this same reasoning, one should know it is proclaimed neither ultimately real nor truly existent.
Second, revealing its own position; first, past conditioned phenomena. Furthermore, what is a past conditioned phenomenon? One whose characteristic has already ceased, whose essential nature has already been relinquished.
Second, present conditioned phenomena. What is a present conditioned phenomenon? One whose characteristic has not yet ceased, whose essential nature has not yet been relinquished, momentarily abiding at the time of its arising.
Third, future conditioned phenomena. What is a future conditioned phenomenon? One whose cause already exists in the present, whose own characteristic has not yet arisen, and whose own essential nature has not yet been attained.

items.title: Section: Why Illusory Things Never Arise, Why Phenomena Don't All Arise at Once, and the Four Conditions Introduced

items.zh: 問：若彼諸行未來本無而得生者，空華、兔角、石女兒等何故不生？答：由空華等無生因故。一切諸行各各差別，定有生因。問：若一切行各各差別有生因者，何因緣故，諸行俱時不頓生耶？答：諸行雖有各別生因，然必待緣方得生起。若彼彼行生緣現前，彼彼行因生彼彼行。是故諸行雖現有因，然無俱時頓生起過。復次，此中云何名諸行因？何等名緣？謂薄伽梵說：諸行生緣略有四種。一、因緣，二、等無間緣，三、所緣緣，四、增上緣。因緣一種，亦因亦緣；餘之三種，唯緣非因。
items.en:
Third, resolving objections; first, explaining originally-absent-now-present; first, the question. Question: if conditioned phenomena, originally absent in the future, can still come to arise, why do a flower in the sky, a rabbit's horn, the child of a barren woman, and the like not arise? Second, the answer. Answer: because such things as a sky-flower lack any cause of arising; every conditioned phenomenon, however distinct from every other, definitely possesses a cause of arising.
Second, explaining why they do not all arise simultaneously; first, the question. Question: if every conditioned phenomenon, however distinct, possesses a cause of arising, for what reason do conditioned phenomena not all arise simultaneously, all at once? Second, the answer; first, clarifying that they await conditions. Answer: although conditioned phenomena each possess a distinct cause of arising, they must still await conditions before they can arise. Second, concluding there is no fault. Whenever the conditions for the arising of this or that phenomenon are present, this or that cause gives rise to this or that phenomenon — therefore, though conditioned phenomena already possess their causes in the present, there is no fault of their all arising simultaneously all at once.
Second, distinguishing cause from condition; first, the question raised. Furthermore, what here should be called the cause of conditioned phenomena, and what should be called their condition? Second, the explanation; first, a brief account; first, stating and listing them. The Blessed One taught that the conditions for the arising of conditioned phenomena are, in brief, fourfold: first, the causal condition; second, the condition of immediate succession; third, the condition of the perceived object; fourth, the condition of dominant influence. Second, a careful distinction. The causal condition alone is both cause and condition; the remaining three are conditions only, never causes.

items.zh: 云何因緣？謂諸色根、根依及識，此二略說能持一切諸法種子。隨逐色根，有諸色根種子，及餘色法種子、一切心心所等種子。若隨逐識，有一切識種子，及餘無色法種子、諸色根種子、所餘色法種子。當知所餘色法自性，唯自種子之所隨逐，除大種色。由大種色二種種子所隨逐故，謂大種種子及造色種子。即此所立隨逐差別種子相續，隨其所應望所生法，是名因緣。復次，若諸色根及自大種，非心心所種子所隨逐者，入滅盡定、入無想定、生無想天，後時不應識等更生，然必更生。

blocks.text: A long day. After short notes on the three gateways and on giving, the treatise takes up a famous debate with the Sarvāstivāda school, who held that past and future things really exist.

Master Cháng Bǎi: concentration can be defiled or undefiled, but the gateway to liberation is only undefiled. 諸行 means conditioned things; the mind should dwell in emptiness to depart from craving. Of the six practices, the first three go with the three wisdoms, the last three with the three liberations.
The recipient's giving and the giver's giving. Master Cháng Bǎi: receiving is also a kind of giving. Its fruit: great wealth, and a disposition to give more.

Master Cháng Bǎi: Sarvāstivādins hold all three times real, citing action and result, and the fact that past and future can be known. On "moving from a future place into the present": what was called future becomes present once conditions ripen.
What has not arisen cannot die. Master Cháng Bǎi: function rests on characteristic; if both are real, both should function. The future has no location; no one sees it anywhere.
The past: characteristic ceased, nature relinquished. The future: its cause exists now; it has not yet arisen.
Illusory things never arise: they lack a cause. Things do not all arise together: they must await conditions.

The causal condition: the physical faculties and consciousness together hold the seeds of all things. Seeds of form follow the faculties; seeds of every consciousness follow consciousness. If the body held no seeds of mind, then after the attainment of cessation, the attainment without perception, or the heaven without perception, consciousness could never arise again; "yet it certainly does".
The debate can seem technical, but it bears on practice. If the past were real now, it could not be let go. Because only the present moment is real, change is possible.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish the gateway from what gives rise to it?
options: the gateway is undefiled only; what leads to it is contaminated hearing, reflection, and cultivation before seeing
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: concentration can be either, but the gateway is only undefiled; what leads to it is contaminated wisdom before seeing.

quiz.q: "Across all such practice." Is 諸行 practice here, and what does Master Cháng Bǎi say of this?
options: 諸行 are conditioned things, not practise; this is dwelling in emptiness, far from craving
quiz.why: 諸行 means conditioned things. Master Cháng Bǎi: the mind should dwell in emptiness to depart from craving.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi map the six correct practices?
options: the first three to hearing, reflection, cultivation; the last three to the three liberations
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the first three go with the three wisdoms, the last three with the three liberations.

quiz.q: What does hearing-wisdom need besides understanding, and what of reflection?
options: hearing needs faith; reflection sometimes uses words, sometimes meaning alone
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: hearing-wisdom adds faith; reflection sometimes relies on words, sometimes on meaning.

quiz.q: What are the two kinds of giving?
options: the recipient's giving and the giver's giving
quiz.why: The recipient's and the giver's giving. Master Cháng Bǎi: receiving is also a kind of giving.

quiz.q: What are the two fruits of giving?
options: great wealth; the resulting predisposition towards its enjoyment
quiz.why: Great wealth and its outflow predisposition. Master Cháng Bǎi: this firm understanding drives further giving.

quiz.q: What view is refuted, and what are its reasons?
options: Sarvāstivādins: all three times are real, since deed and result differ in time and past and future can be cognized
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: Sarvāstivādins hold all three times real, citing deed and result and the cognizability of past and future.

options: moving from its place in the future into the present
quiz.why: Moving from a future place into the present. Master Cháng Bǎi: what was called future becomes present once conditions ripen.

options: what has not yet arisen cannot die
quiz.why: What has not arisen can't die. Master Cháng Bǎi states the opponent's view: the future dies and the present arises.

options: function is conventionally based on characteristic; if both have equally real characteristics, both should function
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: function rests on characteristic; if both are real, both should function.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the refutation of moving between places?
options: the future has no place; no one can see where it is, so how could it move?
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the future has no location; no one sees it anywhere.

quiz.q: How is a past conditioned phenomenon defined?
options: its characteristic has ceased, its nature relinquished

quiz.q: How is a future conditioned phenomenon defined?
options: its cause exists now; its own characteristic hasn't arisen, nature not attained
quiz.why: Its cause exists now; it has not yet arisen.

quiz.q: If things arise from nonexistence, why not sky-flowers and rabbit horns?
options: they lack a cause of arising

quiz.q: If all have causes, why don't they arise at once?
